paper.note: paper-raised #faf7f0 and paper-sunk #e7e0d2 are the shipped steps of this ramp.

ink.note: ink-soft #5a544a (6.42:1 on paper) and ink-faint #6b6355 (5.08:1) are the shipped steps.

steel.note: Bench rail, notebook spines, shelf fixtures. on-steel-soft #c6c9ce measures 4.90:1 here.

felt.note: A region-scale field colour, only the Course Library today. on-felt-soft #b4bcaf measures 5.39:1 here.

brass.note: 2.90:1 on paper — fills and rules only, never text on paper.

brass-ink.note: The text-grade sibling of brass. 5.62:1 on paper. Also the caret and the focus ring on paper.

brass-wash.note: Current row, quiet-control hover, prose note, and ::selection on paper.

fail.note: Faults and failing tests only. Never an accent.

pass.note: Passing tests, a completed Lesson, a sound Tutor verdict. Never an accent.

display.purpose: The one big line a station is allowed: the Brief's question, a Lesson title, the closed Course's Topic.

headline.purpose: Station status lines and the Course Library heading.

title.purpose: A notebook's Topic, a Lesson prose heading, a Syllabus entry.

body-small.purpose: Exercise prompts, agent replies, supporting copy. The Tutor panel steps down once more to 0.875rem.

label.purpose: The machine voice: every count, state, unit, section name, button caption and metadata line. Applied as the `label` utility class.

code.purpose: Code blocks, inline spans, Course Folder paths, Source labels, filenames.

shadows.name: bound-object
shadows.purpose: A bound notebook standing on the felt shelf. The only shadow on a content object.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The Syllabus contents popover under the station header. Ink-tinted, never neutral black.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: The Tutor sheet lifting off the bottom edge below xl.

shadows.name: machined-inset
shadows.purpose: A pressed rail button. Metal is seated into its housing, never floating above it.

shadows.name: bezel-inset
shadows.purpose: The lamp bezel and the notebook spine well.

shadows.name: nameplate
shadows.purpose: The engraved brass nameplate on the rail: contact shadow plus a top highlight.

shadows.name: lit-brass
shadows.purpose: The agent lamp filament. The one glow in the system.

motion.name: ease-desk
motion.purpose: The only easing token. Fast start, long settle — the way a drawer closes.

motion.name: duration-color
motion.purpose: Every colour transition on a control.

motion.name: duration-machined
motion.purpose: A machined transform: the nameplate lift, the toggle knob.

motion.name: duration-sheet
motion.purpose: The Tutor sheet rising below xl.

motion.name: duration-lift
motion.purpose: A notebook lifting 6px on hover or focus.

motion.name: duration-lesson-land
motion.purpose: A generated Lesson arriving in the Generating list.

motion.name: duration-progress
motion.purpose: The brass Progress ribbon growing along a notebook's foot.

motion.name: keyframes-lamp
motion.purpose: The working pulse, shared by the lamp, live State Chips and the writing row.

motion.name: keyframes-land
motion.value: @keyframes land { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(0.75rem) } to { opacity: 1; transform: none } }

motion.name: keyframes-sheet
motion.value: @keyframes sheet { from { transform: translateY(4%); opacity: 0 } to { transform: none; opacity: 1 } }

motion.name: stream
motion.value: 260 characters per second on requestAnimationFrame, trailed by a solid brass block cursor
motion.purpose: The app's one authored motion. Every agent that speaks reveals text this way.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global collapse. Any new motion must survive it without losing meaning.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Page padding steps up; the Rail widens 56px to 64px; the Lesson stepper joins the header line.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The Syllabus station splits into outline and Generator chat.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: The Tutor docks as a 23rem margin panel; Lesson and Tutor scroll independently.

narrative.overview:
Dolphin is one workbench. A steel bench rail runs the full height of the far left; everything to its right is whatever the Course State has clamped in the bench right now — the Course Library, the Brief, the Syllabus, the Generating run, a Lesson, or the closed Course. The rail is the only permanent furniture in the app. There is no sidebar of Lessons, no file tree, no breadcrumb trail: a Course is a thing being worked on, not a folder being browsed.

The materials are literal and few. Warm laid paper carries reading. Precise ink carries text. Brushed steel is the bench edge. Wool felt is a field colour used at region scale — the Course Library shelf is felt wall-to-wall, not a felt panel floating on paper. Brass is the single accent: Progress, live state, the lamp, the nameplate, the cursor that trails streaming text. Each material carries a hairline grain drawn with repeating gradients — a tooth you feel at reading distance, never a decorative texture wash.

Separation is done with hairline rules and seams, never with cards. Corners are square by default; the only radii in the system are the 2-3px chamfers of machined parts and full rounds on genuinely round objects. Depth is reserved for objects that are physically on the desk — a bound notebook, a popover, a summoned sheet. Flat regions of the interface cast nothing.
keyCharacteristics: One workbench; the Course State selects the station, the Student never navigates to one.
Hairline rules and seams do all separation. No cards.
Square by default; 2-3px only where something is machined.
Literata sets every reading surface; JetBrains Mono sets every label, number, path and code span, and nothing else.
One brass accent, used sparingly and never as body text on paper.
Light-only. There is no dark theme, and felt and steel are materials, not a dark mode.
Fully offline: both faces are self-hosted variable fonts, no CDN, no remote assets.

rules.name: The Brass Ink Rule
rules.body: Brass (#B58234) is 2.90:1 on paper — it fails as text and always will. Any brass-coloured word, number or icon-with-a-word on a paper surface uses brass-ink (#7E5518, 5.62:1). Reserve brass itself for fills, rules, ribbons and glows, where contrast ratio does not apply. On felt or steel the sibling is brass-bright. This is the one colour trap in the system; every new surface must clear it.

rules.name: The One Metal Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent hue. If a new surface needs to mean live, current, progressing or the agent is working, it says so in brass. It does not introduce a second accent, and it does not borrow pass or fail — those two mean a test result and nothing else.

rules.name: The Region Colour Rule
rules.body: Felt and steel are materials at region scale, not surface treatments. A felt region fills its whole scroll container edge to edge and carries .on-dark so selection, focus ring and scrollbar re-theme with it. Never a felt card on paper, never a paper card on felt.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is confined to labels, numbers, paths and code. If it is a sentence a person reads, it is Literata. If it is a value a machine produced, it is JetBrains Mono. There is no third face and no display face.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading columns are capped and centred: 46rem for a Lesson, 44rem for the Brief, 38rem for a chat thread or the closed Course. A station that has no measure cap is not finished.

rules.name: The Heading Air Rule
rules.body: More space above a heading than below it — a Lesson prose heading takes 44px above and 16px below; a Lesson section takes 56px above. The gap belongs to the section that is starting, not the one that ended.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No kicker or eyebrow line above them, and no section numbers in prose. The mono section labels in a Lesson (Concept, Examples, Exercises) are the Lesson's own fixed structure named once, not decoration.

rules.name: The Objects-Only Rule
rules.body: If it is a region of the interface, it is flat and separated by a hairline. If it is an object on the desk, it may cast a shadow. A panel that lifts is a card, and this system has no cards.

rules.name: The Seated Metal Rule
rules.body: Steel and brass are seated with inset shadows and a hairline highlight, never with an outer drop shadow. Metal in this world is bolted to the bench.

rules.name: The Square Default Rule
rules.body: New elements are square. A radius must be justified as either a machined part (2-3px) or a genuinely round object (full). It looked softer is not a justification.

rules.name: The Silhouette Rule
rules.body: A notebook's proportions carry data: spine width encodes Lesson count (11-22px), cover height encodes Time Budget (296-362px). Two notebooks of the same size are the same size of Course. Do not add decorative variation to a shape that already means something.

rules.name: The Progress Rule
rules.body: Progress is always a brass rule along an edge — 3px along a notebook's foot, a fill height on the rail spine. It is never a filled wash behind text, never a ring, never a percentage badge on a coloured pill. The number may accompany the rule; it never replaces it.

rules.name: The Stamped State Rule
rules.body: Course State is a bordered mono stamp. Its only variable is live versus static — brass-ink for a Course the agents are working on, faint ink for one they are not. Never one hue per state.

rules.name: The Honest Progress Rule
rules.body: Long work shows what landed, not that something is happening. Generating lists every Lesson in the Syllabus and resolves them in sequence. The only spinner in the build is inside a button that is already labelled with what it is doing.

rules.name: The One Authored Motion Rule
rules.body: useStream is the app's signature motion: text reveals at 260 characters per second on requestAnimationFrame, trailed by a solid brass block cursor, and it is used everywhere an agent speaks — the Generator, the Tutor, Written Exercise feedback, a failing test's hint. Do not add a second reveal idiom.

dos: Do use brass-ink (#7E5518) for any brass-coloured text on paper, and brass-bright (#D2A252) for it on felt or steel. Plain brass is fills and rules only.
Do separate with 1px rule hairlines and seams; use rule-soft for repeated rows inside a single list.
Do cap every reading column (46rem Lesson, 44rem Brief, 38rem thread) and centre it.
Do put more space above a heading than below it.
Do set every label, count, unit, path and code span in the label or code mono roles, and everything a person reads as a sentence in Literata.
Do give a felt or steel region the .on-dark class so selection, focus ring and scrollbar re-theme with the material.
Do apply a material's grain utility together with its background colour (felt-grain bg-felt, paper-grain bg-paper, steel-grain bg-steel).
Do pair every disabled control with a label line saying what would enable it.
Do name the problem and then the recovery in every Fault; state which parts of the app still work.
Do take icons from lucide-react at 11-20px, stroke 1.6-2.4.
Do route all agent text through useStream.
donts: Don't build a card. No shadowed, filled, rounded container for a region of the interface — a bordered hairline rectangle is the container in this system.
Don't put a shadow on anything that is not an object on the desk (a notebook, a popover, a sheet, or seated metal).
Don't introduce a second accent hue, and don't press pass or fail into service as an accent — they mean a test result.
Don't hue-code Course State. It is a stamped mono chip whose only variable is live versus static.
Don't render Progress as a filled wash behind text, a ring, or a badge. It is a brass rule along an edge.
Don't add a radius above 3px. Square is the default; full rounds are for genuinely round objects.
Don't set a sentence in JetBrains Mono, or a label, count or path in Literata.
Don't add an eyebrow or kicker line above a heading, and don't number sections in prose.
Don't ship a chat bubble. Turns are a brass left rule for the Student and plain prose for the agent.
Don't replace honest progress with a spinner. A spinner is allowed only inside a button that already says what it is doing.
Don't load a font, icon set or image from a CDN. The app must render identically with no network.
Don't build a dark theme. Felt and steel are materials in a light interface; the document declares color-scheme: light.
Don't reintroduce a sidebar of Lessons. The Rail carries the Course Library, the open Course and the lamp; the Syllabus lives in the station header's contents popover.
